title: Flavokawain A Attenuated Chronic Kidney Disease: Evidence From Network Pharmacology and Experimental Verification.
authors: Talati, Yugant Krishnakumar; Dagar, Neha; Gaikwad, Anil Bhanudas
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究黄酮类化合物FKA对慢性肾病的保护作用，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a silent global epidemic affecting ~700 million people worldwide, contributing to rising mortality rates. Despite the variety of underlying causes, renal fibrosis is the key pathological feature of CKD. Flavokawain A (FKA), a natural chalcone, is thought to offer protective effects against CKD through its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-fibrotic properties. This study aims to investigate the therapeutic potential of FKA against CKD, using network pharmacology (NP), molecular docking analysis, and In Vivo validation. GeneCards, SwissTargetPrediction, and SuperPred databases were utilized to identify therapeutic targets related to CKD and FKA. Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) were performed using the STRING database. Gene ontology and pathway enrichment analyses were performed with DAVID databases, followed by network construction in Cytoscape. For validation, molecular docking studies were performed using PyRx and tested at doses of 50 mg/kg and 100 mg/kg (p.o.) for 21 days using a unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) rat model. The study identified 109 therapeutic targets for FKA in relation to CKD, highlighting 11 hub targets and 78 potential pathways. Molecular docking showed strong binding efficacy with nuclear factor kappaB subunit 1 (NF-kappaB1) and matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9). In vivo validation supported these findings, as FKA administration showed protective effects on kidney function and histology with the downregulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) markers, such as fibronectin (FN) and transforming growth factor beta1 (TGF-beta1), along with reduced expression of NF-kappaB1 and MMP9. These findings indicate that FKA could be a valuable therapeutic candidate for managing CKD by targeting NF-kappaB1 and MMP9.
abstract_zh: 慢性肾脏病（CKD）是一种无声的全球性流行病，影响全球约7亿人，并导致死亡率上升。尽管病因多样，肾纤维化是CKD的关键病理特征。Flavokawain A（FKA）是一种天然查尔酮，被认为通过其抗炎、抗氧化和抗纤维化特性对CKD提供保护作用。本研究旨在利用网络药理学（NP）、分子对接分析和体内验证，探讨FKA对CKD的治疗潜力。利用GeneCards、SwissTargetPrediction和SuperPred数据库识别与CKD和FKA相关的治疗靶点。使用STRING数据库进行蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPIs）分析。利用DAVID数据库进行基因本体论和通路富集分析，随后在Cytoscape中构建网络。为验证，使用PyRx进行分子对接研究，并在单侧输尿管梗阻（UUO）大鼠模型中，以50 mg/kg和100 mg/kg（口服）剂量给药21天进行测试。研究确定了FKA与CKD相关的109个治疗靶点，突出11个枢纽靶点和78条潜在通路。分子对接显示与核因子κB亚基1（NF-kappaB1）和基质金属肽酶9（MMP9）具有强结合效力。体内验证支持这些发现，因为FKA给药对肾功能和组织学表现出保护作用，下调细胞外基质（ECM）标志物，如纤连蛋白（FN）和转化生长因子β1（TGF-beta1），同时降低NF-kappaB1和MMP9的表达。这些发现表明，FKA可能通过靶向NF-kappaB1和MMP9，成为管理CKD的有价值治疗候选药物。
